newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: IBM sees 6-mo loss, announces restructure.
newsitem.headline: IBM sees 6-mo loss, announces restructure.

text.p: IBM South Africa Ltd said on Wednesday it expects to show a substantial trading loss for the six months' period ending June 30, 1997.
At the same time the group announced it will restructure to improve focus on higher growth areas in a bid to better its competitiveness.

The computer firm said in a published announcement that the restructuring will make it more efficient as it lead the move toward network computing, which links information technology users throughout the world.

"It is top priority to restructure our business as quickly as possible so that we can more effectively bring the global solutions and resources of IBM to our customers," said recently -appointed managing director Sal Faso.
He said that added to the trading loss in the interim period, there will be further costs associated with the restructuring.
Shareholders were advised to take cognisance of this when dealing in the company's shares. They will be appraised of developments concerning the restructuring in due course, the statement said.

IBM earnings for the year ended December 31, 1996 fell 27 percent to 73.8 million rand following the unsuccessful introduction of a new low-tier personal computer product. The product has been withdrawn.
